A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REAL study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mistral and Qwen experiments in Table 2, hyperparameter ablations, training dynamics and an appendix comparison with JEPO.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a regression-reward control, pairwise experiments and ArenaHard 2.0 evaluations.

M1.justification: The REAL objective, generalized policy gradient, RLOO stabilization and Algorithm 2 remain unchanged. Appendix C adds a limited adaptation that takes response pairs and predicts their score difference shifted by +5 into [1,9], extending the original pointwise inputs and targets.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original pointwise coverage and adds Preference Collection training and evaluation on Preference-Bench, HHH Alignment, MT-Bench Human Judgement and Auto-J for pairwise prediction. Appendix D additionally evaluates ArenaHard 2.0 across three newer response-model families. This substantially broadens the evaluated tasks and data.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 4 add Standard RL(reg), using a squared-error reward on decoded scores, alongside the existing accuracy-reward RL baseline. The original comparison methods, including the appendix JEPO comparison, are retained.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce Qwen3-1.7B pairwise training, shifted difference targets and preference accuracy using threshold 5. ArenaHard evaluation introduces agreement counts out of 750 against GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.5 across three response families. These are substantial additional protocols; the original experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new regression-reward control tests whether replacing binary rewards with squared error suffices without REAL's distribution-dependent formulation. Existing hyperparameter ablations, initialization comparisons, training-dynamics plots and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice; algorithmic variance reduction is unchanged.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, ablation and JEPO scores are unchanged. Substantial new results include Standard RL(reg) correlations of 63.4/62.6/50.1 in Table 4, pairwise HHH accuracy of 76.9% for REAL versus 75.6% for TRACT in Table 12, and ArenaHard agreement counts in Table 13. These are additional results under new comparisons and settings, not improvements to v1's reported scores.

T1.justification: The correlation-optimality and generalized-policy-gradient lemmas, assumptions and derivations are unchanged. The proofs move from Appendix B to Appendix E with corresponding renumbering.

C1.justification: The central claims about regression-aware RL, generalized policy gradients, correlation optimality and improved generalization remain unchanged. The abstract drops the detailed Qwen3-32B gains, but those claims remain in the introduction, Figure 3 and Table 2.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly limits applicability to pointwise evaluation; v2 replaces that boundary with pairwise applicability and discussion of continuous targets and wider score ranges. It adds supervision-quality and calibration limitations, and Section 5.2 argues that gains require distribution-dependent rewards rather than regression rewards alone. These substantially expand the applicability and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link, Preference Collection access information and a computational-cost appendix. It newly reports 200/500 training steps for 7B/32B models, GPU hours, memory utilization and qualifications for cross-method cost comparisons. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that retained training budgets changed.

R1.justification: New benchmark references include Askell et al. (2021) and the ArenaHard work by Li et al. (2024b). The positioning relative to RAFT, TRACT, JEPO and other earlier methods remains substantially unchanged; the existing extended related-work discussion remains in Appendix A.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract edits, adds Sections 5.2 and 5.4 and Appendices B–D, and removes the redundant main-text Related Work section while retaining Appendix A. It also adds acknowledgements and updates publication information. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Four new tables display the reward control, computational costs, pairwise results and ArenaHard results. Existing tables are renumbered or repositioned, and Algorithm 2 moves onto a separate page. The original figures and the overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the regression-reward control addresses a useful comparison gap, while pairwise and ArenaHard experiments broaden empirical support and the code/compute disclosures improve transparency. These benefits outweigh limited reporting weaknesses: the new results lack uncertainty estimates, and Table 4's claim that the baseline fails to improve on SFT conflicts with its slightly higher displayed correlations. The net improvement is useful but bounded.
